analyst_view.overall: Early view: Sporting, seventh, return to El Molinón after losing 1-2 to Valladolid there despite 20 shots, and should have Juan Otero back once his ban is served at Real Sociedad II. Las Palmas, under Albert Sánchez since late October per one report, have Jesé and Sandro Ramírez available. Both play in round 14 first.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly higher: Sporting's last four league games averaged three goals, and Las Palmas's last four had five, one, three and four. Sporting's home attack, with Otero back, should be stronger than it was against Valladolid.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. I lean higher: Sporting had 63 per cent of the ball and 20 shots in their last home game, the kind of dominance that piles up corners, and Nicolás Larcamón's side should take a similar approach here.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards. Las Palmas collect cards steadily (32 yellows and two reds in 12 games per LaLiga's figures), which the site already reflects, and this is not a derby or a high-risk fixture, so I see no reason to move it.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. I lean higher: Sporting took 20 on their own against Valladolid at El Molinón, and Las Palmas under their new coach have played open games (3-2 at Oviedo). A total in the high twenties is plausible.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target and I keep it. Sporting's volume has not turned into accuracy (one goal from 20 shots last time), so I do not follow the shots lean all the way.
